_doc: Single source of truth for what each runtime CAN do. Runtime facts only — which events it emits, what it calls them, how it is configured. Kit policy (which hook handles which event) lives in EVENTS in scripts/generate_runtime_hooks.py.
_why: This table used to exist three times: RUNTIME_EVENTS in generate_runtime_hooks.py (codex, grok only), cek_runtime_supports() in scripts/cek_runtime.sh (all four), and the event table in docs/runtime-capability-matrix.md (all four). Three copies cannot disagree safely, and Cursor was absent from the one that actually validates anything — so the guard that caught .codex/hooks.json shipping three events Codex does not have could never fire for Cursor.

Every runtime carries `source` and `verified`. That is not decoration: the v4 plan's first draft was built on a January 2026 blog post about Gemini CLI, a product Google had shut off three months earlier. A capability claim with no date and no URL is a claim nobody can re-check.
_events_format: `events` maps CANONICAL event name -> the name THIS runtime uses. They are equal where the runtime follows Claude Code's naming. A canonical name absent from the map means the runtime does not emit that event. `native_extra` lists events with no canonical equivalent that the kit deliberately uses anyway.

claude._generated_config_note: hooks/hooks.json is hand-maintained: Claude Code is the reference runtime and the manifest carries events no other runtime has, plus per-event async choices that are policy rather than capability.
claude.inject: stdout on SessionStart / UserPromptSubmit / UserPromptExpansion / PostModelSwitch, or hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext
claude._timeout_note: SessionEnd shares a 1.5s budget that a plugin's own `timeout` cannot raise. Not a per-hook ceiling, so it is not expressible here — session-end.sh detaches instead.

cursor._note: Cursor emits literal preToolUse / postToolUse as well, but the kit uses beforeShellExecution / afterFileEdit for the same coverage — see the 'deliberately unused' list in the capability matrix. The canonical mapping below reflects the events the kit actually binds.

codex.inject: stdout or hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext on SessionStart / UserPromptSubmit / SubagentStart
codex._output_limit_note: Model-visible hook output over ~2500 tokens is spilled to <temp_dir>/hook_outputs/<session_id>/<uuid>.txt and replaced with a preview. Tune per handler with additionalContextLimit.

grok.inject: none — stdout is ignored on every event except PreToolUse's decision JSON
grok._timeout_note: Default is 5s, not 30. Only the SessionEnd entry sets an explicit timeout, so every other Grok hook runs against 5s. The session-start chain has not been profiled against that ceiling.
grok._blocking_note: PreToolUse is the ONLY blocking event; exit 2 denies. Everything else fails open.
grok._also_reads_note: Grok reads BOTH, including Cursor's camelCase event names. .claude/settings.json declares no hooks since v3.0.0; .cursor/hooks/_common.sh exits early when GROK_* is in the environment. Without that guard every Grok session ran the kit twice.
